title: Edge signal curation — pocket notes
content:
Purpose Quick personal scratchpad for small, repeatable micro-protocols that we can apply to noisy rows before they go to human labelers. Focus: low-risk transformations that reduce annotator confusion and improve consistency for longtail edge signals. Not a final guide — capture ideas to convert into a short tooling script or quick PR. Principles (mental model) - Do minimal irreversible changes: prefer annotations or normalized copies (e.g., __normalized_text) rather than overwriting source if possible. - Document every heuristic with a short example and confidence level (high/medium/low). - Prefer conservative whitelist operations for high-impact fields (PII, legal, money). - Keep idempotency in mind: running the microprotocol twice should not keep changing the text. Common problem classes observed recently 1) Composite IDs mashed with punctuation: "ABC/123-FF" or "abc#123" -> annotators split into multiple tokens, wrong entity spans. 2) Inline click-tracking garbage appended to URLs: long query params + tracking tokens. 3) Parenthetical noncanonical notes: e.g., "Model X (deprecated)" or "qty: 3 (approx)". 4) Units written as ranges or free text: "10-12kg", "~5lbs", "5kg approx". 5) Phone and numeric id fuzz: spaces, dots, country codes, leading zeros. 6) Embedded HTML/markdown: stray
, **bold**, URL markdown. Microprotocols (quick; name, rule, example before -> after, confidence) - protocol: compact-id-cleanup rule: remove non-alphanumeric separators inside IDs but keep case and hyphen if explicit part of id pattern. Only run when field labeled candidate_id. Idempotent: strip separators once. example: "ABC/123-FF" -> "ABC123-FF" confidence: medium - protocol: url-query-trim rule: strip known tracking query params (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, mc_cid) and any >4 param pairs; leave path and main query useful params (id, ref). If too many params after strip, replace entire query with "?TRUNC" and surface length flag. example: "https://site.com/p?q=1&utm_source=x&fbclid=Z" -> "https://site.com/p?q=1" confidence: high - protocol: inline-note-lift rule: if parentheses contain a single short token from whitelist (deprecated, approx, old, beta) move into metadata flag __note_flags: ["deprecated"]. Remove the parenthetical from main text. example: "Widget 2 (deprecated)" -> "Widget 2" + __note_flags:["deprecated"] confidence: medium - protocol: range-normalize rule: turn short numeric ranges into canonical tuple strings when both bounds parse as numbers. Use same unit if present. Keep original in __raw_field for audit. example: "10-12 kg" -> "(10,12)kg" stored in __weight_norm; tag __norm_source:range-heuristic confidence: low (watch international decimal separators) - protocol: phone-canonicalize rule: remove non-digit characters, keep leading + if present, but do not assume country. If digits length matches local pattern, store as +1-prefixed for US only when region field == US. Otherwise store digits-only in __phone_norm. example: "+1 (415) 555-1212" -> "+14155551212" or "(415) 555-1212" -> "4155551212" confidence: medium - protocol: strip-html-markdown rule: remove angle-tag fragments and common markdown wrappers (**, __, `) but preserve inline code segments surrounded by backticks into __code_snippets. Replace
and

with single space. example: "Price: **$5**
note: `deprecated`" -> "Price: $5 note: `deprecated`" + __code_snippets:["deprecated"] confidence: high Decision heuristics for whether to auto-normalize or send to human - Auto-normalize when: the transformation is reversible or additive (stores __raw_field), confidence high, and pattern matches a small deterministic regex with <=3 groups. - Defer to human when: PII-sensitive fields, numeric ranges with mixed units, ambiguous language, or when normalization reduces interpretability (e.g., dropping currency context). Quick regex candidates (notes only) - id separators: ([A-Za-z0-9])[^A-Za-z0-9]+([A-Za-z0-9]) -> replace with \1\2 (but run only for candidate_id field) - utm strip: ([?&])(utm_[^=&]+=[^&]*) -> remove all occurrences - html tags: <[^>]+> -> replace with space (but keep blocks as special-case) - phone digits: ([+]?)[^0-9]+ -> collapse to digits, preserve leading + if present Examples — sample rows and what I'd do - row1: field: sku_desc = "Pro-Widget / v2 (old)", product_id = "pw-123/45" actions: protocol inline-note-lift -> sku_desc becomes "Pro-Widget v2" + __note_flags:["old"]; protocol compact-id-cleanup -> product_id "pw-12345"; store __raw_product_id. - row2: field: url = "https://a.co/p?ref=abc&utm_medium=email&gclid=XYZ" actions: url-query-trim -> "https://a.co/p?ref=abc"; store __url_query_removed:["utm_medium","gclid"] - row3: field: weight = "~5 lbs" actions: range-normalize -> parse 5 as single value, store __weight_norm:(5)lbs; add flag __approx:true Open questions / TODOs - Create small library function that takes a schema map and microprotocol list; supports dry-run and an "annotate-only" mode that appends __suggested_normalizations but does not modify source. - Decide standard for storing __raw_field names (suffix vs prefix). Proposal: prefix __raw_ + original_field_name. Keep for at least 90 days. - Need a lightweight annotation UI column for human-review to Accept/Reject suggested normalizations. Should be toggled off for high-volume auto-normalizations. - Internationalization: decimal/comma handling, local phone heuristics. Do we infer region from other fields? Add region hints in schema. - Write unit tests for two known noisy customers: CUST-87 (heavy url tracking) and CUST-210 (id formats). Notes to self: - Avoid overwriting original timestamps. If normalization changes tokenization boundaries used by annotators, add short explanation in __audit_note. - Keep a small log of examples where heuristics flipped label outcomes during pilot. We'll need to present metrics (label disagreement delta) before wide rollout. Slack snippets to copy into a PR description "This PR adds three small microprotocols (url-query-trim, strip-html-markdown, phone-canonicalize) plus a dry-run mode that appends suggested normalization fields prefixed with __suggested_. The heuristics are conservative and reversible; default off for PII fields. See JIRA-DF-789 for acceptance criteria and test vectors." End of pocket notes — convert to short RFC or script next when I have bandwidth.
